key_insight: RESCUE uses four specialized LLM agents to implement complementary machine-learning and rule-based EHR screening for potentially missed rare-disease testing candidates.
clinical_relevance: The workflow could help identify patients who may warrant evaluation for exome or genome sequencing, but it does not establish a diagnosis.
method: Ontology Agent organizes clinical data into a four-tier genetic-evidence taxonomy.
Modeling Agent trains a positive-unlabeled XGBoost classifier; Screening Agent applies model-based and rule-based screening.
Review Agent samples clinical notes to assess medical necessity and operational feasibility.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective pediatric-hospital evaluation, holdout AUC was 0.808 (n=12,591); among 175,842 screening-eligible patients, flagged patients were 7.4-fold more likely than controls to receive subsequent genomic assessments, and blinded chart review found 80% precision for appropriate ES/GS candidacy after accounting for prior testing.
watch_item: Single-hospital retrospective findings require prospective, external validation before assuming broader clinical benefit or operational feasibility.
paper_title: RESCUE: An end-to-end multi-agent LLM system for proactive rare-disease patient screening in the EHR
